**Solved Mid‑Term Paper – Web Engineering (SWE‑315)** --- ## Q.1 (2.574 = 10) *Scenario: a simple video‑portal web application that lets registered users buy and download albums.* | # | Diagram / Model | Key Elements & How to Draw (textual description) | |---|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------| | a | **Use‑Case Diagram** | 1. **Actors**: *Unregistered User*, *Registered User*, *Administrator* (optional).
2. **Use‑Cases**:
• *Register* (Unregistered → Registered)
• *Login* (Unregistered → Registered)
• *Search Album* (Both)
• *View Album Details* (Both)
• *Buy Album* (Registered)
• *Download Album* (Registered, only if purchased)
• *Recharge Credit* (Registered)
• *View Account* (Registered)
• *Logout* (Both)
3. **Relationships**:
• *Include*: *Login* → *Search Album* (search only after login).
• *Extend*: *Buy Album* → *Recharge Credit* (if insufficient balance). | | b | **Activity Diagram (Buying an Album)** | 1. **Start** → 2. *User selects album* → 3. *System shows album detail* → 4. *Check purchase status* → 5a. *If already bought → show “Download”* → 5b. *If not bought → show “Buy”* → 6. *User clicks “Buy”* → 7. *System checks credit balance* → 8a. *If sufficient → deduct price, mark album as purchased, show “Download”* → 8b. *If insufficient → prompt “Recharge Credit”* → 9. *End*. | | c | **Content Structure Model** | 1. *Home Page* – search box, navigation links.
2. *Search Results Page* – list of albums (title, artist, price).
3. *Album Detail Page* – title, artist, track list, price, “Buy” or “Download” button.
4. *Account Page* – credit balance, purchase history.
5. *Login / Register Page* – form fields. | | d | **Navigation Structure Model** | 1. **Top‑bar**: *Home*, *Search*, *Account*, *Login/Logout* (always visible).
2. **Breadcrumbs** on detail pages: *Home > Album Title*.
3. **Footer**: links to *Terms*, *Privacy*, *Contact*.
4. **Dynamic links**: “Buy” or “Download” appear based on purchase status. | --- ## Q.2 (3 × 2.5 = 7.5) | # | Question | Answer | |---|----------|--------| | a | **Which framework or library would be suitable for the scenario?** | **React** (or Vue/Angular). React is lightweight, component‑based, and works well for a single‑page application that needs dynamic UI updates (e.g., showing “Buy” vs. “Download”). | | b | **What kind of web application would you create, SPA or MPA?** | **Single‑Page Application (SPA)** – all interactions happen on one page; only data is fetched via AJAX, giving a smoother user experience. | | c | **List down client‑side and server‑side languages which you may use while developing this application.** | **Client‑side**: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3 (with a pre‑processor like SASS).
**Server‑side**: Node.js with Express (JavaScript), or alternatively Python (Django/Flask), Java (Spring Boot), or C# (.NET Core). | --- ## Q.3 (3 × 2.5 = 7.5) | # | Question | Short Answer | |---|----------|--------------| | a | **How does JavaScript perform Type Coercion/Type Casting?** | JavaScript does *implicit coercion* when operators need a specific type (e.g., `1 + "2"` → `"12"`). It also has *explicit casting* via constructors (`Number("5")`, `String(true)`) or unary `+`/`!`. | | b | **Write web‑related solution for given problem occurring during web application development: if budget overruns or failure to meet business objectives?** | Adopt *Agile* practices: split work into small sprints, hold daily stand‑ups, use burn‑down charts to track budget, and perform *continuous integration* to catch defects early. If objectives slip, conduct a *scope‑review* with stakeholders, re‑prioritize backlog items, and consider *feature toggles* to release core functionality first. | | c | **Explain any method of elicitation and negotiation in requirements collection process.** | **Prototyping**: build a low‑fidelity mock‑up and let stakeholders interact with it. **Solved Paper – 2023 Mid‑Term – Web Engineering** --- ### Q.1 – Brief Answers (4 × 2.5 = 10 pts) **A. Guidelines for successful Web‑application development** 1. **Requirements & User‑Centric Design** – gather clear functional & non‑functional needs; involve real users. 2. **Modular Architecture** – separate concerns (presentation, business logic, data access). 3. **Responsive & Accessible UI** – use fluid layouts, semantic HTML, ARIA roles. 4. **Security & Privacy** – validate inputs, use HTTPS, protect credentials, follow OWASP guidelines. 5. **Performance & Scalability** – cache static assets, minify resources, use CDNs, load‑balancing. 6. **Testing & Continuous Integration** – unit, integration, end‑to‑end tests; automated pipelines. 7. **Deployment & Monitoring** – containerise, use CI/CD, log, monitor, rollback strategy. **B. SPA vs MPA – key characteristics** | Feature | SPA | MPA | |---------|-----|-----| | Page load | Single HTML page; subsequent navigation via JS | Full page reload for each navigation | | Navigation speed | Very fast after initial load | Slower due to full reload | | SEO | Requires prerendering or SSR | Naturally SEO‑friendly | | State management | Client‑side state (Redux, Context) | Server‑side state (sessions) | | Development complexity | Higher JS complexity | Simpler server‑side routing | | Use‑case | Rich interactive apps (mail, dashboards) | Content‑heavy sites (news, e‑commerce) | **C. Contextual vs Non‑contextual links** - **Contextual link** – URL contains context (e.g., `/movies/1234`) so the server can directly fetch the resource. - **Non‑contextual link** – generic URL with query parameters or no identifier (e.g., `/movies?search=action`) requiring the server to interpret the request. **D. Explicit type conversions in JavaScript** 1. **Number()** – converts value to a number (e.g., `Number('42')`). 2. **String()** – converts value to a string (e.g., `String(42)`). 3. **Boolean()** – converts value to a boolean (e.g., `Boolean('')`). 4. **parseInt() / parseFloat()** – parse numeric strings, optionally with radix. 5. **Unary plus (`+`)** – quick numeric conversion (e.g., `+'42'`). --- ### Q.2 – Working of the WebML diagram (Insert Comment page) 1. **User selects a movie** → the system retrieves the movie’s ID (`MovieID`). 2. **Insert Comment form** is displayed with a textarea for the comment and a submit button. 3. **On submit**: - The form data (`UserComment`) is sent to the server via an HTTP POST. - The server creates a new `Comment` entity linked to the `Movie` (`MovieID`) and the `User` (`UserID`). 4. **Feedback**: After successful insertion, the page refreshes or updates the comment list to show the newly added comment. --- ### Q.3 – UWE Modelling (10 pts) #### a. Content Structure Model - **Entities** - `User` (id, username, email, password, role) - `Movie` (id, title, year, description, genre, photo) - `Person` (id, name, birthday, birthplace, photo) - `Theatre` (id, address, showrooms, performances) - `Comment` (id, text, rating, timestamp, user_id, movie_id) - `Ticket` (id, seat, showtime, price, user_id, movie_id, theatre_id) - `Favorite` (user_id, movie_id) - **Relationships** - `User` – 1..* `Comment` (one user can comment many times) - `User` – 1..* `Ticket` - `User` – 1..* `Favorite` - `Movie` – 1..* `Comment` - `Movie` – 1..* `Ticket` - `Movie` – 1..* `Person` (cast/crew) - `Theatre` – 1..* `Performance` – 1..* `Ticket` #### b. Navigation Model - **Top‑level pages** 1. **Home** – search bar, featured movies. 2. **Movies** – list + filter; each movie links to its *Movie Detail* page. 3. **People** – list; each person links to *Person Detail* page. 4. **Theatres** – list; each theatre links to *Theatre Detail* page. 5. **Login / Register** – authentication pages. 6. **My Account** – profile, favorites, purchase history. - **Secondary pages** - *Movie Detail* → tabs: Overview, Cast, Soundtrack, Reviews, Buy Ticket. - *Person Detail* → Biography, Filmography. - *Theatre Detail* → Address, Showrooms, Upcoming Performances. - *Ticket Purchase* → Seat selection, payment. - **Navigation flow** 1. Unregistered → Home → Search → Movie Detail → Register/Login → Buy Ticket. 2. Registered → Home → Search → Movie Detail → Comment / Rate → My Account. --- ### Q.4 – Welcome‑Message Page (5 pts) ```html Welcome Page
